data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'dolor', meaning 'sorrow' or 'pain'. In Christian tradition, the name Doloritas may symbolize the suffering and sacrifice of Jesus Christ and the sorrows of the Virgin Mary. The name Doloritas carries the meaning “Sorrowful, sorrows” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Doloritas usually hope their child will grow to embody sorrowful, sorrows and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Doloritas holds a deep cultural significance in the Christian faith, representing the deep sorrow, pain, and sacrifice that Jesus Christ endured for humanity. This name may be given as a reminder of the Passion of Christ and the price of redemption. It can also serve as a reminder of the suffering that the Virgin Mary experienced as she witnessed the suffering and death of her Son.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Doloritas holds profound meaning, representing the willingness to endure suffering for the sake of love and redemption. This name may be given to a child as a reminder of the suffering and sacrifices made by Jesus Christ and the Virgin Mary, and as a call to embrace one's own suffering with faith and trust in God. It serves as a reminder of the role of suffering in the Christian faith and the ultimate triumph of love and redemption over pain and sorrow.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Doloritas: The Sorrowful One. Symbolically representing the deep sorrow and empathy felt by those who carry the burdens of others. Spiritually, Doloritas embodies the compassionate and nurturing aspect of the Divine Mother.
